ideas.ablation_behavior_off: V_i := 0 for every item, so rho_i := 0 and D_i^2 = d_P^2 exactly; the code then runs the unmodified hyperbolic RQ assignment and reconstruction with identical codebook size, schedule and loss weights.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full run, c = 1 Poincare base and V_i from the frozen training-only successor covariance both active in the same argmin and the same reconstruction term. One training run only; the two switched-off configurations exist as flags and are checked on a forward pass, but are not trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: base term replaced by the Euclidean one, d_P^2 -> ||p - mu||^2 and log_p(mu) -> (mu - p), while V_i and rho_i are unchanged, giving a flat Mahalanobis-warped RQ.
ideas.behavior_computation: Training split only. Build directed counts N[i,j] over consecutive pairs in training sequences (25,456 training items). Row-normalise with add-alpha smoothing, alpha = 1/V (documented default), giving P(j|i). Build PPMI = max(0, log(P(j|i) / P_col(j))), truncate to rank 16 via SVD, giving y_i in R^16, each normalised to unit L2. For item i take its top-8 successors by P(j|i), compute the weighted centroid c_i = sum_j p_j y_j and deviations e_j = y_j - c_i, and set Vhat_i = [sqrt(p_1) e_1, ..., sqrt(p_8) e_8] in R^{16x8}. Frozen once.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions from training sequences only, summarised per item as its successor distribution and the successor covariance directions.
ideas.cost_estimate: Marginal per-step cost is one d x r projection per (item, code) pair inside the assignment loop. At the frozen scale, ~1023 items per step (24556/24), 3 levels, K=256 codes, d=64, r=8 gives 1023*3*256*(64 + 8*64) ~ 0.5 GFLOP per step, on the order of 5-8 percent of one step's encoder+decoder work, hence ~5-8 percent wall-clock over 72,000 steps (3000 epochs x 24). One-off precompute: sparse PPMI over the training transition graph (24556 items), truncated SVD rank 16, then a 16x16 rank-8 eigendecomposition per item; minutes on CPU, frozen before Stage 2. No extra backward pass (V_i detached).
ideas.coupling_equation: D_i(p, mu)^2 = d_Poincare(p, mu; c=1)^2 * ( 1 + ||V_i^T log_p(mu)||^2 / ((tr(V_i V_i^T) + eps) * ||log_p(mu)||^2 + eps) ), with V_i = W Vhat_i, W in R^{64x16} trainable and Vhat_i frozen training-only successor covariance.
ideas.coupling_path: item -> frozen PPMI successor covariance Vhat_i (behaviour) -> learned alignment W -> per-item basis V_i -> trace-normalised anisotropy rho_i(p,mu) computed on the tangent residual log_p(mu) -> warped distance D_i -> argmin over the level codebook AND the reconstruction term -> chosen code sequence (k_1..k_L) -> Stage 2 parameter updates and downstream the SID vocabulary consumed by Stage 3. Setting V_i = 0 collapses rho_i to 0 and both the argmin and the loss become exactly plain Poincare RQ; setting curvature to flat keeps the same rho_i but on Euclidean distances, so both the chosen codes and the gradients change. Neither switch can be removed without changing the core computation.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behaviour anisotropy aligns with the latent directions along which next-item identity varies, the quantizer spends finite codebook on those directions, items sharing a successor profile share more prefix tokens, H(sid_2|sid_1) and H(sid_3|sid_1,sid_2) drop, and Stage 3 test recall@10 moves above 0.065 in the single frozen run. Kept if the measured successor-prefix agreement and Stage 3 test_recall@10 both improve over the recorded baseline.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside quantization: in the assignment distance that selects mu_{l,k} at every residual level l = 1..L, and in the reconstruction/commitment term that scores the final prefix point against the item. It therefore acts on the whole prefix hierarchy, not on one level.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (ball radius 1), Poincare distance d_P(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))), and the Mobius log/exp maps log_p, exp_p used for the residual chain; the metric is warped by the behaviour term, D_i^2 = d_P^2 * (1 + rho_i).
ideas.key_change: Each training item receives a frozen, training-only successor-covariance basis V_i (rank r, trace-normalised so the anisotropy budget is exactly one Euclidean dimension); the RQ assignment and its reconstruction term use D_i^2 = d_Poincare^2 * (1 + rho_i), where rho_i in [0,1] is the normalised alignment of the tangent residual with V_i.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Transition counts, the PPMI SVD and the per-item covariance read only training-split sequences; validation and test sequences are never touched, so no validation/test interaction can enter the frozen Vhat_i. The codebook sees V_i only through the training quantizer loss, and the Stage 3 evaluator never feeds behaviour back into SID construction. Items whose only evidence is a validation or test occurrence keep the smoothed table entry, which was computed without them.
ideas.motivation: Two items with the same content but different futures currently get SIDs from content geometry alone, so the next-item generator cannot use the one thing that predicts the next token: where the user's behaviour goes from this item. A plain RQ-VAE allocates codebook resolution isotropically; behaviour says which residual directions actually matter.
ideas.novelty: The earlier mechanisms relocate or reweight codebook points (successor-Frechet centroids, radial placement from context entropy, per-level curvature, successor geodesic shift, cone constraints, Lorentz profile smoothing). BEHMET-RQ leaves the codebook points and their update rule unchanged and makes the DISTANCE ITSELF behaviour-anisotropic: a per-item, trace-normalised covariance of the item's successor directions is inserted multiplicatively into the Poincare distance used for assignment and reconstruction, so the curved metric spends finer effective resolution along the directions in which that item's behaviour varies. The warp is bounded in [1,2] by construction, so no coupling weight exists to tune.
ideas.observables: (a) assignment: for behaviourally diverse items the per-level code histogram shifts toward codes whose tangent offsets align with V_i, and successor-prefix agreement (fraction of consecutive training pairs whose SIDs share >=1 and >=2 leading tokens) rises; (b) gradient/parameter: codebook points move along behaviour-varying directions, visible as increased projection of codebook displacement onto span(W); (c) predictability: H(sid_2|sid_1) and H(sid_3|sid_1,sid_2) drop on held-out training sequences; (d) Stage 3 test recall@10 in the single frozen run.
risks: The PPMI successor basis may be only weakly related to the latent space, so the learned alignment W degenerates into an arbitrary rotation and the warp becomes near-isotropic noise, leaving recall flat. The +rho sign (extra distance, hence extra resolution, along behaviour-varying directions) is argued from rate allocation and could be backwards for this data. Items with concentrated successors (rho near 1 on one direction) may over-fragment prefixes for popular items. The bounded 2x loss dynamic range could mildly interact with the learning rate.
ideas.safeguards: clamp every point to radius (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c) before log/exp; add 1e-8 inside every squared-norm denominator; clamp rho into [0,1] (analytically bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz, the clamp only absorbs float error); set V_i := 0 whenever the item has fewer than 2 distinct successors or its covariance trace is < 1e-8, making that item's assignment exactly plain Poincare; declare D2 infinite for codes producing a non-finite log map; keep c fixed at 1 so the conformal factor 1/(1-c||x||^2) never blows up; detach Vhat_i and unit-normalise every y_i so the warp is invariant to the arbitrary PPMI-SVD scale.
ideas.spec_equations:
# one-off, training split only, frozen
  P[j|i] = (N[i,j] + 1/V) / (sum_j' N[i,j'] + 1)
  PPMI[i,j] = max(0, log( P[j|i] / (sum_i' N[i',j] / sum_{i',j'} N[i',j']) ))
  Y = svd_trunc(PPMI, rank=16);  y_i = Y[i] / (||Y[i]|| + 1e-12)
  top8(i) = first min(8, nnz_i) successors by P[j|i] desc
  c_i = sum_{j in top8(i)} P[j|i] y_j / sum_{j in top8(i)} P[j|i]
  Vhat_i = concat_j [ sqrt(P[j|i]) * (y_j - c_i) ]      # 16 x min(8,nnz_i), zero if nnz_i = 0
  # per step
  x = encoder(item)                      # in ball, ||x|| <= (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c)
  p = x; loss = 0; commit = 0
  for l in 1..L:
      for k in 1..K:
          u   = log_p(mu[l,k])
          dP2 = poincare_dist2(p, mu[l,k], c)
          rho = ||V_i^T u||^2 / ((trace(V_i V_i^T) + 1e-8) * ||u||^2 + 1e-8)
          rho = clamp(rho, 0.0, 1.0)
          D2[l,k] = dP2 * (1.0 + rho)
      k* = argmin_k D2[l,k]
      u  = log_p(mu[l,k*])
      r  = log_p(x)
      loss   += lambda_l * D2[l,k*]      # warped reconstruction of this level
      commit += ||r - u||^2
      p = exp_p(r - u)                   # hyperbolic RQ residual update
  loss += beta * commit
  # switches: phi_behavior=0 -> V_i := 0 ; phi_geometry=0 -> dP2 := ||p-mu||^2 and log/exp := flat affine
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the item's encoder point x in the curvature-1 Poincare ball, the level codebooks mu[l,1..K] in the ball, and the frozen per-item successor covariance Vhat_i plus trainable W. Outputs: the discrete SID (k_1..k_L), the warped per-level reconstruction loss and commitment term, and gradients with respect to encoder parameters, codebooks and W.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. Encoder output x_i lies in the Poincare ball of fixed curvature c=1; at level l the query point is the running prefix point p_{l-1}; the code is argmin_k D_i(p_{l-1}, mu_{l,k})^2; the residual is carried by log/exp maps at p_{l-1}; loss = sum_l lambda_l * D_i(p_l, x_i)^2 + beta * commitment, with lambda_l and beta unchanged from the baseline RQ-VAE (they are not part of this mechanism).

ideas.title: Behaviour-warped Poincare metric inside residual-quantizer assignment and reconstruction

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The same code with the transition table disabled: m(p_l) := p_l for every prefix, so every geodesic triangle is degenerate, delta_l = 0, R = I, and the quantizer reduces to the plain hyperbolic RQ. No other change.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run exactly as specified: training-only successor means build m(p_l), the curved triangle gives delta_l, and R(delta_l) rotates the residual at every RQ level. Nothing is ablated and nothing is tuned in this run; the switches exist in the code for later diagnosis but only this arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The same code with c = 0: exp/log become identity, d_c becomes Euclidean squared distance, the law of cosines is replaced by the flat one giving zero defect, and delta_l := 0 with R = I. Behaviour statistics are still computed and still attached, they simply cannot act.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, build a sparse table count(i -> y) over next-item pairs inside a window of 5 in each training sequence. Set w(i,y) = count(i,y) / sqrt(pop(i) * pop(y)) with pop(x) the total training occurrence count (a cosine/popularity normalisation with no free parameter). The per-item successor point is m_i = argmin_{m in B} sum_y w(i,y) d_c(m, e_y)^2, solved by K=3 Karcher fixed-point iterations m <- exp_m( sum_y w(i,y) log_m(e_y) / sum_y w(i,y) ) from m = e_i, using the current detached item embeddings. The prefix successor point is m(p) = exp_0( sum_{i in C(p)} w_i log_0(m_i) / sum_i w_i ) with w_i = out-degree of i in the training transition graph and C(p) the items assigned prefix p at the previous epoch's snapshot. Items with no training successors take m_i = e_i; prefixes with fewer than two members or with m(p) within 1e-3 of p take delta = 0.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions inside training sequences (the immediate next items within a forward window of 5 positions), turned into a normalised transition weight and then into a per-prefix successor mean point in the Poincare ball.
ideas.cost_estimate: The frozen scale is 24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch (about 1023 items/step), 3000 epochs, four cards, one run. Per step the extra work is about 1023 x 4 levels x (3 distances + 3 angle evaluations + one 64-dim 2-plane rotation) ~ 8e6 flops, roughly 1-3 percent of a transformer step, plus a small autograd node count because of the exp/log maps. The per-epoch prefix-cluster successor refresh is 24556 log/exp evaluations plus 4 aggregations, under a second. Per-item successor means are precomputed once at epoch 0 and refreshed every 100 Stage-2 epochs from detached embeddings (about 7e5 exp/log each refresh, tens of seconds total). Expected wall-clock overhead 2-5 percent; the 3000-epoch budget, the frozen Stage-3 protocol and the single run are unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: r'_l = R( delta_c( O, p_l, m(p_l) ) ) * log_{p_l}(z), with delta_c = pi - ( alpha_O(c, a, b, d) + alpha_P(c, a, b, d) + alpha_M(c, a, b, d) ), a = d_c(p_l, m(p_l)), b = d_c(O, m(p_l)), d = d_c(O, p_l); behaviour enters only through m(p_l) from the training transition table, curvature enters only through the sqrt(c)-scaled law of cosines and the metric d_c, and the product R(delta) * log_{p_l}(z) is the single term in which they meet.
ideas.coupling_path: z -> p_l -> successor mean m(p_l) taken from the training transition table -> geodesic triangle (O, p_l, m(p_l)) -> angle defect delta_l under curvature c -> rotation R(delta_l) -> rotated residual r'_l -> nearest code k_l -> SID prefix p_{l+1} -> Stage-3 generation. Removing behaviour sets m(p_l) = p_l, the triangle degenerates and delta_l = 0 so R = I. Removing geometry sets c = 0, so the defect is c * area = 0 and R = I as well; the same removal also replaces exp/log/d_c with their Euclidean counterparts. The rotation therefore exists only when both factors are present, and one connected pathway carries both into the code index.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the RQ tangent frame at a prefix is rotated toward the direction of that prefix's training-transition successors, deeper codes should become more behaviour-predictable and the generative recommender should place the true next item inside its top-10 beam more often. The keep condition is that on the single run the Stage-3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065, with the recorded diagnostics showing (i) a measurable churn in level>=1 code assignments, (ii) an increase in prefix-to-successor top-1 predictability on training prefixes, and (iii) no collapse of codebook usage. If recall is flat while delta_l is empirically near zero for most prefixes, the behaviour means are too close to the prefix and the idea is not doing anything.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer, at every RQ level, after the residual r_l = log_{p_l}(z) is formed and before the nearest-code search; the rotation changes the code index and therefore the straight-through gradient and the SID prefix, and it also runs in the forward pass of the reconstruction loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball model of constant negative curvature -c with c = 1 fixed by the unit-ball normalisation (no curvature sweep). Curved operations used: Mobius addition, exp_p / log_p maps, geodesic distance d_c, the curvature -c hyperbolic law of cosines for triangle angles, the Gauss-Bonnet angle defect delta = pi - (alpha_O + alpha_P + alpha_M), and the resulting SO(2) holonomy rotation R(delta).
ideas.key_change: At every RQ level the residual r_l = log_{p_l}(z) is rotated by R(delta_l), where delta_l is the angle defect of the geodesic triangle O-p_l-m(p_l) under curvature -c and m(p_l) is the training-transition successor mean of the items currently sharing prefix p_l. The rotated residual, not the raw one, is compared with the level codebook, so the chosen code (and therefore the whole downstream prefix) depends jointly on behaviour and curvature.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition table, the popularity counts, the per-item successor means and the per-prefix means are built exclusively from the training split's user sequences; validation and test interactions are never read, and the Stage-3 protocol only consumes the frozen SID table produced by Stage 2. No validation or test user, item or transition enters the curvature, the behaviour means, the frame construction or the code assignment. The per-epoch refresh uses current model parameters and the same frozen training transition weights, so it is a training-time statistic, not a data leak.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE prefixes are learned purely from reconstruction, so two items with the same prefix can have completely different training-time next items. A generative recommender then emits a prefix whose continuation distribution is behaviourally incoherent. The problem is that nothing in the quantizer knows where the prefix actually leads. This idea makes the prefix's own training-transition successors define a second, curved path from the origin to the prefix, and lets the curvature-induced mismatch between the direct path and the behaviour-detour path rotate the residual that selects the next code. Prefixes therefore become frames aligned with their behavioural future rather than only with reconstruction.
ideas.novelty: The operator is a pure curvature invariant, the Gauss-Bonnet angle defect (holonomy) of the geodesic triangle (origin, prefix point, behaviour successor mean), applied as an SO(2) rotation of the residual tangent vector before the nearest-code search. Earlier work here coupled behaviour through codebook centroids (Frechet), per-level curvature scalars, radial/rank assignment, cones, and first-order embedding shifts; none used a frame/holonomy term, and none sits at the level of the residual's tangent frame. The rotation is exactly zero both in flat space and when the behaviour point collapses onto the prefix, so the behaviour term and the curvature term are not two additive losses but a single multiplicative interaction that exists only when both are on.
ideas.observables: (i) per-level SID churn: fraction of items whose code at level l changes relative to the uncoupled quantizer, expected to be near zero at level 0 only if the root collapses and clearly nonzero at levels 1 and above; (ii) prefix-to-successor top-1 predictability of training prefixes under a held-out-transition probe, which should rise if the rotation aligns frames with behaviour; (iii) codebook usage entropy and collision rate as health checks; (iv) the primary judgement, Stage-3 test Recall@10 against the 0.065 target on the single frozen-protocol run.
risks: (a) delta_l may be near zero for most prefixes, making the rotation a no-op; (b) delta_l near pi/2 for a minority could over-rotate and scramble otherwise good codes; (c) the successor mean is dominated by globally popular continuations unless the count normalisation suppresses them; (d) rotating the target on its geodesic sphere changes only assignment, not the reconstruction target, so the codebook may keep its old geometry and the gain may be limited; (e) adding a behaviour statistic per epoch adds a moving target that can slow convergence inside the fixed 3000 epochs.
ideas.safeguards: project every encoder output and every codebook entry to ||x|| <= (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c) after each update; clamp artanh arguments to 1-1e-7 and cosh arguments to at most 20; set delta = 0 whenever any of sinh(sqrt(c)a), sinh(sqrt(c)b), sinh(sqrt(c)d) is below 1e-6, whenever ||log_0(p_l)|| < 1e-3, whenever ||wperp|| < 1e-3, or whenever the prefix cluster has fewer than two members; take the principal defect min(delta, pi-delta) and clamp to [0, pi/2] so the rotation never exceeds a quarter turn; assert | ||r'_l|| - ||r_l|| | < 1e-6 because R is orthogonal in the conformal coordinate frame and the Poincare metric factor is isotropic; stop-gradient on delta_l and on m(p_l) so no gradient is taken through acosh or through the transition statistics; fall back to m_i = e_i for items with zero training successors; if a NaN appears in delta, reset it to 0 for that step and continue rather than aborting the run.
ideas.spec_equations: c=1. x (+) y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2)x + (1-c||x||^2)y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2). exp_0(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v/(sqrt(c)||v||); log_0(x)=artanh(sqrt(c)||x||) x/(sqrt(c)||x||). exp_p(v)=p (+)( tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_p ||v||/2) v/(sqrt(c)||v||) ), lambda_p=2/(1-c||p||^2). log_p(x)=(2/(sqrt(c) lambda_p)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-p)(+)x||) ((-p)(+)x)/||(-p)(+)x||. d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||). Law of cosines: cos alpha_O = (cosh(sqrt(c)b)cosh(sqrt(c)d) - cosh(sqrt(c)a)) / (sinh(sqrt(c)b)sinh(sqrt(c)d)), and cyclically for alpha_P and alpha_M with the opposite side in the first factor replaced appropriately. delta = pi - (alpha_O+alpha_P+alpha_M); delta <- min(delta, pi-delta); delta <- clip(delta, 0, pi/2). u = log_0(p_l)/||log_0(p_l)||; wperp = log_0(m) - <log_0(m),u>u; w = wperp/||wperp||; R = I + sin(delta)(w u^T - u w^T) + (cos(delta)-1)(u u^T + w w^T). r_l = log_{p_l}(z); r'_l = R r_l; k_l = argmin_k d_c(exp_{p_l}(r'_l), e_{l,k}); p_{l+1} = p_l (+) e_{l,k_l}. Successor means: w(i,y)=count(i,y)/sqrt(pop(i)pop(y)); m_i from K=3 iterations m <- exp_m( sum_y w(i,y) log_m(e_y) / sum_y w(i,y) ); m(p)=exp_0( sum_{i in C(p)} w_i log_0(m_i) / sum_i w_i ), w_i = out-degree(i). Total loss unchanged (RQ reconstruction + commitment + codebook) except that codes and prefixes are the rotated ones.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs per item per level: the item embedding z in B^d_c, the current prefix point p_l in B^d_c, the prefix successor mean m(p_l) in B^d_c (or p_l itself when the behaviour switch is off), and the level codebook {e_{l,k}} in B^d_c. Outputs: the scalar holonomy angle delta_l, the rotated tangent vector r'_l in R^d (same hyperbolic norm as r_l), the selected code index k_l, and the next prefix point p_{l+1}; and, when the switch is off, delta_l = 0 and r'_l = r_l.

specification.text: Poincare ball B^d_c with fixed c=1 (embeddings projected to ||x|| <= (1-eps)/sqrt(c)); exp/log/Mobius-add as usual. For each level l: p_0 = g = Frechet mean of training item embeddings; r_l = log_{p_l}(z); m(p_l) = exp_0( sum_{i in C(p_l)} w_i log_0(m_i) / sum_i w_i ); compute a=d_c(p_l,m), b=d_c(O,m), d=d_c(O,p_l); angles by the curvature -c law of cosines; delta_l = pi - (alpha_O + alpha_P + alpha_M), principal value clamped to [0, pi/2]; build the orthonormal 2-frame u = log_0(p_l)/||log_0(p_l)||, w = orthonormalised part of log_0(m) orthogonal to u; r'_l = R(delta_l) r_l with R = I + sin(delta)(w u^T - u w^T) + (cos(delta)-1)(u u^T + w w^T); code k_l = argmin_k d_c(exp_{p_l}(r'_l), e_{l,k}); p_{l+1} = p_l (+) e_{l,k_l}. All delta and m values are stop-gradient; gradients flow through r_l in z and p_l.

ideas.title: Geodesic-holonomy residual rotation: the behaviour successor mean bends the RQ tangent frame by the curvature angle defect

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: a_l := 0 for all l and q is never read, so x_{l+1} = x_l and every level quantises the ordinary hyperbolic residual; basepoints may be logged but never enter the computation.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run above, the only arm trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: exp/log/Mobius/d_P replaced by Euclidean counterparts (arithmetic weighted mean for b, L2 distances, linear blend c + (1-a)(x-c) + a(b-c)); behaviour still enters through b and a.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: in every training session, every consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) increments n(u_t,u_{t+1}); p(j|i) = n(i,j)/sum_j n(i,j) after dropping self-pairs. For level l+1 and item i, q_{l+1}(j|i) = (1/|G_l(i)|) sum_{i' in G_l(i)} p(j|i'), where G_l(i) is the set of training items sharing the first l codes with i (G_0(i)={i}); the basepoint uses the top M=16 entries of q.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed within-session item transitions (successor distribution p(j|i)), aggregated to SID prefix level.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step (batch 1023, L=4, d=64): 4x1023 exp/log pairs plus 4x1023 Mobius sums ~12k curved ops, under 1 ms on one card, under 5% of baseline step time. Per epoch (24 steps, 24556 items): prefix-bucket hashing 24556x4 keys (~0.1 s) plus basepoint refresh 24556 items x 5 levels x M=16 neighbours x 5 Karcher iterations x d=64 ~5e8 flops (~0.05 s). Over 3000 epochs the refresh is the only recurring addition, ~1.5e12 flops total (minutes), on the same four cards with stop-gradient.
ideas.coupling_equation: x_{l+1,i} = exp_{c_l}( (1-a_{l,i}) log_{c_l}(x_{l,i}) + a_{l,i} log_{c_l}( b_{l+1,i}(q) ) ), with a_{l,i} = d_P(x_{l,i}, c_l) / ( d_P(x_{l,i}, c_l) + d_P(c_l, b_{l+1,i}(q)) + eps ) and b_{l+1,i}(q) = argmin_m sum_j q_{l+1}(j|i) d_P^2(m, z_j).
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour -> q_{l+1}(.|i) -> top-M -> weighted Karcher mean b_{l+1,i} in the ball -> log_c(b_{l+1,i}) in the geodesic blend -> transported residual x_{l+1} -> code choice k_{l+1} -> SID prefix -> Stage 3 tokens. One chain, no side losses: zeroing the behaviour term sets a_l=0 and degenerates to standard hyperbolic RQ; replacing the curved ops with Euclidean ones degenerates to a linear residual blend.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the successor basepoint is a genuinely useful conditioning signal, levels 2..4 stop encoding pure reconstruction error and start encoding which successor branch the item belongs to: P(next item's level-l code | first l codes) rises at l=2..4 versus a plain hyperbolic RQ, and the single both-on run exceeds Stage 3 test_recall@10 = 0.065. If prefix predictability rises but recall does not, the generative model is not exploiting the reallocated bits and the idea should be dropped.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual-quantiser recurrence at every level l=1..L (L=4), inside the reconstruction loss d_P(z, MobiusSum(c_1..c_L))^2, and inside the per-epoch basepoint Frechet mean (stop-gradient).
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed curvature c=1 (sectional curvature -1) with Mobius addition a(+)b, exp_x(v) = x (+)( tanh(sqrt(c)||v||/2) v/(sqrt(c)||v||) ), log_x(y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||) ((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||, d_P(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||); the Frechet mean is the Karcher fixed point m <- exp_m( sum_j w_j log_m(z_j) ).
ideas.key_change: After each level's code is chosen, the residual is replaced by the point on the Poincare geodesic running from that code to a successor-Frechet basepoint of the item's prefix bucket, blended by error/(error+behaviour gap), and that point is what level l+1 quantises.
ideas.leakage_boundary: p is estimated only from consecutive pairs inside training-split sessions; validation and test sessions never touch n(.,.), never define G_l, never define a basepoint. Prefix buckets come from the model's own assignment of TRAINING items only. No validation or test item enters the codebook, the basepoints, any training SID, or any gradient.
ideas.motivation: A generative recommender consumes SID prefixes as tokens, so what matters is that an early prefix already narrows the plausible NEXT item. A plain residual quantiser spends levels 2..L on the reconstruction error of the item's own embedding, which is behaviour-blind: two items in the same prefix bucket with disjoint successor sets keep diverging down branches that carry no transition information.
ideas.novelty: The earlier rounds moved the codebook centroids (Poincare-Frechet successor codebook), the per-level curvature scalar (CURVCTRL-SID), or the radial rank of the assignment (BRad-RQ). SUCC-CHART-RQ keeps the codebook shared and unmoved and keeps curvature fixed at c=1; it changes the POINT AT WHICH THE RESIDUAL IS EXPRESSED (basepoint of exp/log), chosen per item and per level from the successor distribution of that item's current PREFIX bucket, and it transports the residual along a geodesic with a weight equal to the error-to-signal ratio, so there is no coupling hyperparameter to tune.
ideas.observables: (i) prefix-successor diagnostic P(level-(l+1) code of the true next item | first l codes) for l=1..3 must rise; (ii) codebook usage at levels 2..4 shifts toward successor-discriminative directions (entropy of q inside each code); (iii) mean hyperbolic reconstruction error stays within a small factor of plain RQ; (iv) Stage 3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.
risks: (1) The behaviour pull corrupts the reconstruction objective, so decoder item identification degrades and nets out negative. (2) Prefix buckets are coarse and noisy early in training, making the basepoint meaningless for the first few hundred epochs; the origin warm start must be fixed a priori, not tuned. (3) Long-tail items with no successors fall back to the origin and gain nothing. (4) Poincare arithmetic near the boundary yields NaNs under mixed precision. (5) Single-run seed noise can swamp a 0.001-0.003 recall effect.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||z||, ||x||, ||c|| to <= 0.999 before artanh; compute artanh via torch.atanh on a value clamped to 1-1e-6; add eps=1e-7 in every Mobius denominator; set a=0 when g<1e-6 or q is empty (b=0); fall back to basepoint 0 for items whose prefix bucket has zero transition mass; stop-gradient on b and on bucket assignment; initialise the codebook with radius <= 0.5; keep codebook and residual tensors in float32 even under AMP; assert finite loss every 100 steps.
ideas.spec_equations:
c=1, eps=1e-7, radius clamp 0.999.
ball(v) = tanh(||v||) v/||v|| with ||v|| clamped to [1e-8, 0.999].
Mobius: x(+)y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2) x + (1-c||x||^2) y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2).
Epoch refresh (stop-grad): z_i = ball(enc(i)); for l=1..L: G_l(i) = items sharing the first l codes; q_{l+1}(j|i) = mean over G_l(i) of p(j|.); S = TopM(q); b_{l+1,i} = Karcher(z_S, q(S)/sum q(S)).
Step: for l=1..L: k_l = argmin_k d_P(x_l, C[l,k]); c = C[l,k_l]; g = d_P(c, b_{l+1,i}); e = d_P(x_l, c); a = e/(e+g+eps) if g>1e-6 else 0; a = clamp(a,0,1); x_{l+1} = exp_c((1-a) log_c(x_l) + a log_c(b_{l+1,i})).
Loss: L = mean_i d_P(z_i, MobiusSum_l C[l,k_{l,i}])^2 + 0.25 * mean_i sum_l d_P(x_{l,i}, C[l,k_{l,i}])^2, the 0.25 being the baseline's documented default commitment weight, unchanged and untuned.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder outputs z_i (batch, d), codebooks C[1..L] (K, d) in the ball, sparse successor table p, current prefix buckets, curvature c=1. Outputs: per item the code tuple (k_1..k_L) that is the SID, plus transported residuals x_2..x_{L+1} used for the next level's assignment and for the loss.

specification.text: Directed within-session training transitions give p(j|i). The level-(l+1) basepoint b_{l+1,i} is the weighted Poincare (Karcher) Frechet mean of the ball-mapped encoder outputs of the top-M=16 successors of the level-l prefix bucket of i. Geometry: fixed curvature c=1 Poincare ball, Mobius addition, exp/log at the chosen code, geodesic interpolation, hyperbolic reconstruction distance. Coupling: x_{l+1} = exp_c((1-a_l) log_c(x_l) + a_l log_c(b_{l+1,i})), a_l = d_P(x_l,c)/(d_P(x_l,c)+d_P(c,b_{l+1,i})+eps). Switches B (behaviour off) and G (geometry off) exist in code; only both-on is trained.

ideas.title: Successor-anchored exponential chart: every RQ residual is geodesically re-expressed at a behaviour-derived prefix-successor basepoint

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: conc_j = 0 for all j so w_j = 0; then x'_j = x_j and v'_j = z_j bit-exactly, the pipeline reduces to the plain RQ-VAE and the SIDs equal the baseline ones. The switch exists and is unit-tested for exact identity; it is not trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full geodesic transport, the arm actually trained once for 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: v'_j = R*((1 - w_j) z_j/R + w_j log_0(s_j)), the same behaviour weights and successor consensus but a flat chord in tangent coordinates with the metric factor removed; this tests whether the curved path, not merely the behaviour pull, carries the gain.
ideas.behavior_computation: From every training sequence, count directed pairs (u_t = j, u_{t+1} = k) into N_jk; n_k = training interaction count of k; adjust Ntilde_jk = N_jk / n_k; keep the top K = 20 successors by Ntilde, renormalize to P_j; conc_j = max(0, 1 - H(P_j)/log K) when j has at least 2 kept successors and 0 otherwise; m_j = sum_k N_jk; m_med = median of m_j over items with m_j > 0. All of N, m_med, P, conc are computed once before Stage 2 and frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Successor branching concentration combined with a measured outgoing-transition support, computed per item from directed consecutive-item transitions in the Stage 2 training split only.
ideas.cost_estimate: Adds one exp, one log_x, one exp_x, one log_0 per item (4 elementwise passes over d) plus one sparse gather at the epoch refresh: N*K*d MACs per fixed-point iteration = 24556*20*64 = 31.4M MACs, x3 iterations = 94M MACs per epoch, i.e. 3.9M MACs per step at 24 steps/epoch, under 0.2 percent of a 10M-parameter encoder step at batch 256. Refresh wall clock about 10-20 ms on one GPU once per epoch (3000 refreshes total), transport under 1 ms per step; memory 24556x20 int32 indices (2.0 MB) plus 24556x20 float32 weights (2.0 MB) plus three N-vectors of scalars. Overall under 1 percent wall clock, no change to the Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.coupling_equation: v'_j = R * log_0( exp_{x_j}( w_j * log_{x_j}( s_j ) ) ), with w_j = conc_j * m_j/(m_j + m_med) from the training transition graph and s_j = FrechetMean_{D_c}({x_k}_{k in Succ_K(j)}; P_j), so the transported step length is exactly w_behaviour(j) * d_geodesic(x_j, s_j).
ideas.coupling_path: z -> v = z/R -> x = exp_0(v) -> [s = Fréchet(P, code embeddings), w = conc*m/(m+m_med)] -> x' = exp_x(w log_x(s)) -> v' = R log_0(x') -> RQ levels 1..L -> decoder -> reconstruction loss -> gradient into the encoder. The behaviour scalars (P, conc, m, m_med) enter only through s and w, the curved operations enter only through exp/log and the geodesic, and they meet in the single expression exp_x(w log_x(s)): setting w = 0 removes the behaviour entirely, replacing exp/log by identity makes the same expression a Euclidean chord.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Successor pairs must actually become close in latent space after transport, i.e. the transport must reduce, not increase, the distance between a training item and its successor consensus while leaving content reconstruction intact. Observable: the fraction of test-window adjacent pairs sharing the level-1 SID and the expected matching prefix length must rise relative to behaviour-off, reconstruction loss must rise by less than a fixed small fraction, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed 0.065. If reconstruction loss rises materially while prefix agreement does not, the encoder is cancelling the pull and the idea is dead.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside Stage 2 training, on the forward path between the encoder output and the first residual level of the RQ-VAE, so every one of the L quantization levels and therefore every prefix position is computed on the transported latent; the same map is applied unchanged when SIDs are assigned.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Exponential and logarithmic maps of the Poincaré ball with fixed negative curvature c = 1 (curvature -1), including the position-dependent conformal factor lambda_x and a three-step weighted Fréchet mean, used as the geodesic interpolation exp_x(w log_x(s)).
ideas.key_change: Insert, between the encoder and the residual quantizer, a Poincaré-ball transport step x' = exp_x(w * log_x(s)) whose direction s is the hyperbolically averaged full-prefix code of the item's training successors and whose scalar weight w is the item's successor branching concentration times a measured support shrinkage. The quantizer then sees R * log_0(x').
ideas.leakage_boundary: N_jk, n_k, m_med and the successor lists come only from the Stage 2 training split; the successor-latent consensus s_j is built from the current Stage 2 codebook and from the same training-only x_k, never from validation or test items; validation and test appear only in the Stage 2 selection metric and the frozen Stage 3 protocol, neither of which writes back into the table, the consensus or the transported latent. Items absent from training have conc_j = 0 and receive no transport.
ideas.motivation: Content-only latents place an item next to items that look alike, not next to items a user actually consumes after it, so a generative recommender that emits prefix codes has to spend early prefix bits on content similarity and cannot express "this item leads to that item". Items whose continuation is ambiguous (branching users) and items whose continuation is deterministic need different geometric treatment, but a Euclidean quantizer has one global scale for both.
ideas.novelty: The previous rounds moved the codebook (Fréchet successor means), moved per-level curvature (feedback curvature control) and re-ranked radial assignment (BRad-RQ). None of them transformed the latent that is fed into the quantizer. Here the training-only transition table acts as a vector field, the encoder point is moved along the geodesic joining it to its successors' Fréchet consensus, and the transported point - mapped back to tangent space - is what all L residual levels quantize. The step length is a behaviour-only scalar (branching concentration x transition support) and the path is a behaviour-free object, so the contributions are separable while the computation is one shot.
ideas.observables: (a) mean Euclidean distance between x_j and s_j over training items (must fall relative to behaviour-off at the same epoch); (b) fraction of SID level-1 codes shared by training adjacent pairs and by held-out adjacent pairs; (c) churn of level-1 and level-2 assignments between epoch 0 and the last epoch; (d) reconstruction MSE trend; (e) Stage3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target, with the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches present in the config but only both-on trained.
risks: (1) The encoder can learn to invert the transport, making the pathway a no-op; applying the same deterministic map at SID-assignment time limits but does not remove this. (2) Popularity-adjusted P still concentrates mass on head items, so many items are dragged toward a handful of attractors and level-1 codes collapse. (3) The detached per-epoch consensus lags the codebook and can oscillate. (4) Fixed c = 1 mismatches the latent scale if the encoder's norm distribution drifts, since R is frozen. (5) lambda_x blows up near the boundary and can produce large gradients.
ideas.safeguards: clip all radii with rho_max = (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c) before every exp/log and inside Möbius addition; floor 1 - c||x||^2 at 1e-6 in lambda_x and in every denominator; apply artanh to inputs clipped at 1 - 1e-6; when ||x - s||_g < 1e-8 return x (log gives 0); when an item has fewer than 2 kept successors or m_j = 0, set conc_j = 0 and s_j = x_j so the transport is the exact identity; detach s_j and w_j (no gradient through the transition table or the consensus) and recompute them only at epoch boundaries to avoid oscillation; clamp w_j <= 1 (guaranteed since m_j/(m_j+m_med) < 1); if the epoch-level mean ||v' - z||/||z|| exceeds 1.0, scale all w_j by that ratio for the epoch (a measured, self-limiting normalization, not a tuned constant); keep the RQ codebook and commitment terms byte-identical to the baseline; run the whole transport in float32 even under mixed precision.
ideas.spec_equations: PRE: N_jk from training pairs; P_j = topK(N_jk/n_k) renormalized; m_j = sum_k N_jk; m_med = median(m_j | m_j>0); conc_j = clamp(1 - H(P_j)/log K, 0, 1). R = median_batch ||z|| at epoch 0 (frozen). EPOCH START (torch.no_grad): e_k = sum_{l=1..L} Codebook_l[SID_l(k)]; x_k = exp_0(e_k / R); for each j: s^(0) = x_j; repeat 3 times: s^(t+1) = exp_{s^(t)}( sum_k P_jk log_{s^(t)}( x_k ) ); store s_j, w_j = conc_j*m_j/(m_j+m_med). FORWARD per batch: r = clamp(||z||/R, 1e-6, r_max); v = z/R; x = tanh(r)*v/r; d = log_x(s_j); beta = w_j * d; x' = x (+) tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_x ||beta||/2) * beta/(sqrt(c)||beta||); v' = R * artanh(clamp(sqrt(c)||x'||, 0, 1-1e-3)) * x'/(sqrt(c)||x'||); feed v' to RQ. LOSS unchanged: ||z - Dec(zq(v'))||^2 + commitment + codebook terms. Switch BEHAVIOUR_OFF: w_j = 0. Switch GEOMETRY_OFF: v' = R*((1-w) z/R + w log_0(s_j)).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder output z (B x d), frozen tables {P_jk, conc_j, m_j}, m_med, R, current codebooks and SID assignment, fixed c = 1. Outputs: transported latent v' (B x d) with the same shape and scale as z for the quantizer, plus the per-item (s_j, w_j) cache refreshed once per epoch. No change to the decoder, the RQ-VAE loss or the downstream generative model interface.

specification.text: Poincaré ball D_c = {x in R^d : c||x||^2 < 1}, c = 1 fixed (curvature -1), metric g_x = (2/(1-c||x||^2))^2 I, lambda_x = 2/(1-c||x||^2), exp_0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v/(sqrt(c)||v||), log_0(x) = artanh(sqrt(c)||x||) x/(sqrt(c)||x||), exp_x(v) = x (+) tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_x ||v||/2) v/(sqrt(c)||v||) with Möbius addition (+), log_x(y) = 2/(sqrt(c) lambda_x) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||) ((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||. Per item j and per epoch: x_j = exp_0(z_j / R) with R = median_batch ||z|| measured once at epoch 0 and frozen; s_j = 3-step weighted Fréchet mean in D_c of {x_k : k in Succ_K(j)} (detached); w_j = conc_j * m_j/(m_j + m_med); x'_j = exp_{x_j}( w_j * log_{x_j}(s_j) ); v'_j = R * log_0(x'_j); the RQ-VAE consumes v'_j and reconstructs z_j. Switch BEHAVIOUR_OFF sets conc_j = 0 (hence w_j = 0, hence x'_j = x_j and v'_j = z_j exactly); switch GEOMETRY_OFF replaces the last two lines by v'_j = R*((1-w_j)(z_j/R) + w_j log_0(s_j)) (straight tangent-space chord, no lambda rescaling, no exp/log on the path); switch BOTH_ON is the code above.

ideas.title: Branching-conditioned geodesic transport of the encoder latent before the RQ-VAE quantizer

objective: Improve the semantic IDs of a generative recommender: a training-only behaviour signal must guide the whole SID prefix hierarchy in a hyperbolic RQ-VAE, and the result must raise the Stage 3 test recall above 0.065.
